lesson.subtitle: Lesson 9 -- Did You? Asking About the Past
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Giovanna de Fátima | Lesson 9 -- Did You? Asking About the Past
lesson.grammar_point: past simple questions with did plus the base verb (Did you...? / What did you do?) and the short answers Yes, I did / No, I didn't
phases: Did, and the Verb Goes Back

listenings.text: Hi Giovanna, it is Karen. You sent me five questions for the newsletter two weeks ago and I forgot to answer them. Sorry. Here they are, all five. Question one: I started in this company in two thousand nineteen, in the London office. Question two: no, I did not study engineering first. I studied geology, and I changed after three years. Question three: the last time I was on a big site was in March, in the north of England, and it rained every single day, so I know exactly how your week felt. Question four, the best thing I ever heard from a supervisor: go home, the tunnel will still be here tomorrow. And question five, the difficult one. Did I ever want to stop? Yes, once, in my first winter. I did not stop. Call me on Friday.

Good morning. Ray Collins. Before we start, three questions, and I want three short answers. Number one: who checked the pumps on Friday night? Nobody? Somebody checked them, because the lower area is dry this morning, so I want a name before lunch. Number two: did anybody call the concrete company yesterday? I asked for that call on Thursday and I did not hear anything after that. Number three, and this one is for the whole crew. Last week we lost three days. Did we learn anything, or did we only get wet? Think about it, write me one line, and give it to me on Friday. That is all. Now, the plan for today.

extra_audio.text: Last Tuesday Giovanna interviewed Greg for the site newsletter. First she asked him about the flight, and he said it took eleven hours. Then she asked who he met on his first day, and he forgot every name except one. After that she asked about the rain, and he heard about it in every e-mail. Her last question was about Norway, and that answer was the best one.
